html:
The moment, in Sri Lanka in the 1st century BCE, when Buddhist monks first wrote down the scriptures of the Theravada school. Tradition dates it to around 29 BCE, under King Vattagamani Abhaya of Anuradhapura.

For centuries the teachings of the Buddha had passed by memory alone, recited by groups of monks. The Sri Lankan chronicles say that famine and war threatened the lines of reciters, so monks gathered at Aluvihara and wrote the texts on palm leaves. Buddhism had reached the island with Mahinda's mission two centuries earlier.

The result is the Pali Canon, the Tipitaka or "three baskets": monastic rules, the discourses and the higher teaching. It is the most complete early Buddhist canon that survives. From Sri Lanka it spread to Burma, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia, the heartland of Theravada Buddhism, where it is still the core scripture.
